newsitem.title: USA: Borden Chem to buy BASF acetylene stake.
newsitem.headline: Borden Chem to buy BASF acetylene stake.

text.p: Borden Chemicals and Plastics LP said Thursday that it signed a letter of intent to acquire BASF AG's 50 percent interest in an acetylene plant which is jointly owned by both companies.
Terms of the agreement were not disclosed.
The plant is located in Geismar, Louisiana, where the two companies have adjacent chemical manufacturing facilities.
The acetylene plant has been operated by BCP under the existing joint venture arrangement and its output shared by the two partners.
In a press release, Borden said it plans to use the acetylene made available through the purchase as additional feedstock for its acetylene-based vinyl chloride monomer (VCM) plant.
The company intends to expand the capacity of this VCM plant to help meet its internal requirement for VCM, the raw material used to manufacture polyvinyl chloride resins.
The transaction, which is expected to close December 31, 1999.
A company spokesman said that the reason the closing date is so far off is to give BASF a chance to build its own acetylene plant.
In a related move, Borden will enter into a long-term supply agreement with BASF for anhydrous hydrochloric acid, which is used as a feedstock in BCP's acetylene-based VCM process.
It also will enter into a long-term supply arrangement for off-gas from a new acetylene plant BASF plans to build.
This acetylene off-gas will be used as a feedstock for BCP's methanol production.
